blocker.summary: The full causal chain for the sub_821D6C20 SIGSEGV is now resolved down to a specific, live-verified failure point. sub_821D5F48 (the game's Xenos/renderer bootstrap) has 4 checks that all converge to the same early-failure return if any fails; r442 established the caller (sub_821D7DE0) logs that failure non-fatally via sub_821F5B18 and proceeds regardless, so sub_821D6C20 always runs next and crashes on the unguarded null dereference of the never-constructed object at 0x82935D98. r443 pinpointed exactly which of the 4 checks fails: live breakpoints on all 4 checks' callee functions (plus the known crash entry) showed check 1's callee (sub_821F4078) succeeds repeatedly, check 2's callee (sub_821CC508) fires exactly once, and then execution jumps straight to sub_821D6C20's crash -- checks 3 and 4's callees (sub_821D28C8, sub_821D5600) are never reached at all. A live breakpoint placed exactly on the instruction reading sub_821CC508's return value (found via live disassembly, not static/guessed addressing -- an earlier finish-based attempt gave an inconsistent value, consistent with the already-known ctx.rN offset pitfall) confirmed it returns 0xFFFFFFFF (-1). sub_821CC508 shares its constant argument (0x829ddd80) with sub_821CC008, the function r441 already found enumerates real files by path (open/size/close) -- the calling pattern (loop while 0, fail if negative, succeed if positive) is a textbook async-operation-completion poll, so the working hypothesis is that sub_821CC008 queues a content/file operation against that descriptor and sub_821CC508 polls it, and in this offline environment that operation completes with an error rather than success. Named for r444: decompile sub_821CC508 itself (already disassembled in the ac6-us Ghidra project) to see exactly what condition makes it return -1, and live-trace sub_821CC008 to identify which specific file/path is involved and whether a native host stub (NtCreateFile/NtReadFile, already extensively worked on elsewhere in this project) is the actual cause. The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
